business_rules.statement: The governing rule is separation: the thing that knows when is never the thing that does what.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Scheduled-work architecture, controller and worker are separate identities

business_rules.statement: This architecture does not claim end-to-end exactly-once execution. What it claims is at-least-once delivery of the trigger, at-most-once effect per idempotency key, and a written record of every attempt.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Ledger, lease, fencing token, idempotency key

business_rules.statement: Every scheduled effect passes through the owning business service; no scheduled identity writes directly to a business table.
Every occurrence is a durable row minted before its planned instant, so that a missed moment is detectable.
Every effect carries an idempotency key, and a repeat under the same key produces no second change and a receipt naming the original.
A write submitted under a fencing token lower than the recorded token is refused.
No surface renders an occurrence as successful without an effect receipt.
Every Schedule Definition change produces a new immutable revision and passes its approval path.
A failed precondition ends the occurrence as skipped with a recorded reason, never as failed.
An occurrence is closed only by the reconciliation pass or by a receipt, never by the trigger.

Every transition names a causing identity, human or non-human, and writes an audit event in the same transaction as the transition. No transition may be caused by the absence of something. Terminal states are genuinely terminal.
Pausing a definition suppresses future occurrences without deleting them, and every suppressed occurrence remains visible.
A terminal occurrence is never revived; a replay creates a new occurrence linked to the original.
Every terminal state reaches reconciled, including skipped, expired and cancelled.
Suspension by tenant state cannot be resumed from the scheduling console.

Rule one, narrowing only. A Schedule Definition may narrow authority but never broaden it. A definition that names a broader scope than its identity holds fails validation at approval, not at execution.

Rule two, no borrowed sessions. A scheduled run must not reuse an expired human session or a stale bearer token. Scheduled work acts under its own non-human identity with its own credential lifecycle.

Rule three, privileged operations are governed. Manual trigger, retry, replay, backfill, skip, pause, resume, cancellation, override and quarantine release each require and record role, scope, reason, preconditions, current authorisation, approval where required, segregation of duties, idempotency key, audit event in the same transaction, notification where externally visible, a fallback and a recovery path.
Rule four, tenant reach is limited by the tenant's own settings. Tenant roles hold no authority over platform scheduling machinery.
Rule five, the Read-only Auditor reads and never acts.
Every cell in both matrices carries an explicit status; no cell is blank.
No approver may approve their own submission on any scheduling operation.

The card's field order never changes, and every field is filled; a field that genuinely does not apply says so with its specific reason in the form Not applicable - reason. A schedule with no card is not approvable.

No card contains a cadence, retry limit, timeout, queue limit, offline duration, retention period, confidence threshold, model expiry, approval window or account limit that the Statement of Work does not state, unless it is marked TBD - Client Decision Required with a named decision.
Every card states what its effect explicitly is not.
A definition whose card has an unfilled field cannot be approved.

Store the official instant in Coordinated Universal Time, preserve the governing local time zone as an Internet Assigned Numbers Authority identifier such as America/Chicago, and never derive one from the other after the fact.
Causal ordering is never derived from wall-clock time alone; ordering follows server receipt and the occurrence and fencing sequences.
Every Schedule Definition declares exactly one missed-occurrence policy from the six, and the declaration is part of the approved revision.
A replay of non-idempotent, privileged, safety-sensitive, expired or externally visible work cannot proceed without recorded human review.
The mechanism that fires the timer is never the mechanism that holds the truth. A timer is only permitted to say it is time to look; it is never permitted to say it happened.
Every occurrence has a row in the scheduled-run ledger before any handler runs, and that row is created in the same database transaction as the due-work signal.
No mechanism may be selected that cannot be made idempotent. No mechanism may be selected whose only failure signal is silence.
Artificial intelligence never selects, triggers, skips or re-times a scheduled occurrence. Detection is deterministic; interpretation is agentic.
No definition of authority class A executes through a mechanism that lacks a durable ledger row created in the same transaction as its due-work signal.
Every named product in this section is rendered in the deliverable with the label Recommendation - R&D. A rendering that omits the label fails the build.
No acceptance test anywhere in this chapter asserts against a vendor product name; every test asserts against observable behaviour.
No scheduled-work definition of authority class A uses mechanism class M8, M10 or M11 as its primary mechanism.
Every definition using M3 has a paired M5 definition that owns the platform-side record of the same obligation.
Every definition declares a fallback class or the explicit value no fallback - controlled hold.
Class M3, the Frontline local signed timer, is the only class permitted to enforce anything while the device is offline, and it enforces locally only - it never asserts platform truth.
A lifecycle rule that expires or deletes objects is prohibited on this platform. There is no purge anywhere on the platform; nothing ages out of existence.
Every scheduled occurrence has a ledger row created in the same transaction as its cause, verified by transaction-boundary test.
No surface renders an occurrence as complete unless the ledger row is in a terminal success state.
Every occurrence that produces a device-directed action creates a command record and never advances that record beyond queued without a device acknowledgement.
No storage lifecycle configuration contains an expiration or deletion rule.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Infrastructure policy scan, failing the deployment

business_rules.statement: No artificial-intelligence component appears in any scheduled-work execution decision path.

Exactly one surface owns the official record of any scheduled occurrence; the other four render it. A scheduled occurrence may never grant a surface an authority it does not otherwise hold. A timer is not a role.
Every surface that renders a scheduled occurrence must render its state, not a summary word. Synced is banned as a lone state, and so is done.
No surface may imply an offline tablet received or applied anything.
No surface can be driven into showing an occurrence as applied on a device without a stored device acknowledgement.
A scheduled activation may only move content from approved and released, pending effective date to effective. It may never move content from pending approval to anything.

The evaluation gate is hard, always, and binds every operator including the root. No scheduled occurrence may publish an agent or composed behaviour that has not passed its evaluation scenarios. Sandbox-before-publish is an ENFORCED invariant with no off position.
Due-moment re-validation covers approval validity, evaluation-gate status, sandbox evidence and locale completeness.
No timer exists anywhere in the Lane-B path; the human decision is the sole trigger, and DEC-LANEB-001 is referenced wherever the path is documented.
The ten operational actions are a closed set; no scheduled occurrence creates an eleventh, and no scheduled occurrence performs one of the ten on a human's behalf.
No gate item is ever rendered as decided because a timeout elapsed. A timeout is never rendered as a decision.

Under clock uncertainty, the device resolves toward the restrictive outcome: if it cannot tell whether a deadline has passed, it treats it as passed for anything that grants permission, and as not-yet-passed for anything that would remove a protection.
No worker-facing pace, timer or performance display exists in any module, state or release.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Full user-interface string and component scan across all twelve Frontline modules

business_rules.statement: A parked run never blocks the worker's other assigned runs.

The scheduled time passing proves nothing about the device. No code path may set a device-related state to applied, in force, delivered or acknowledged as a consequence of a clock event alone. Only a message from the device may do that.
All fifteen command states are individually representable, individually renderable and individually queryable; no surface collapses them.
A device that exceeds the offline trust window refuses designated high-risk actions and sign-offs until a successful sync.
The 4-hour critical re-notification clock starts from server knowledge, not from device event time.

THE EXECUTION GATE. If tenant scope, authority, qualification, version, hold state, legal hold, idempotency or official truth cannot be established, the occurrence does not execute. It moves to blocked with a reason class, becomes visibly overdue, and a human is told.
The eight-condition gate runs before every occurrence, with no bypass path, including for governed manual ticks.
No failure path marks an obligation as done, satisfied, applied or closed on an unverified basis.
No failure path bypasses role-based access control, crosses a tenant boundary, bypasses qualification, specification, evaluation, approval, publication, or the Severity 1 hold and release rules.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Security regression suite under every failure condition

business_rules.statement: THE ABSENCE RULE. Alert on the absence of an expected run, not only on an explicit failure. Every SCHED-* definition declares an expected cadence and a tolerance.
THE CARDINALITY RULE. Do not place raw tenant identifiers, worker identifiers, schedule identifiers or scheduled-run identifiers into unbounded metric labels.
THE AUDIT RULE. Observability records do not replace audit evidence. Where a compliance question is asked, the answer comes from audit, always.
Tenants do not receive a scheduler dashboard. Adding a tenant-facing scheduler dashboard is Explicitly prohibited in this design.

THE RULE. Do not recommend automation merely because it is technically possible. Every scheduled-work proposal must name a real business problem, a real person who feels it, and a real consequence if the automation goes wrong.
No definition with a verdict of rejected or prohibited exists in any deployment.
No scheduled occurrence performs any of the ten Client Command Center operational actions autonomously.
No gate item transitions to a decided state through a timeout in any code path.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Exhaustive timeout test at both configured values

business_rules.statement: THE TWO ABSOLUTE RULES. Audit events must never become hidden employee surveillance. Artificial intelligence must never automatically make a disciplinary or employment decision. Neither rule has an exception, a configuration, a tier gate or an override.
business_rules.applies_to: Every scheduled process and every artificial-intelligence capability

business_rules.statement: No scheduled process may create, materialise or persist a per-worker behavioural feed, time series or ranking.
No per-worker no-show or lateness tally exists in any store, report or scheduled process.
No artificial-intelligence component produces an output whose stated or implied subject is an individual worker's performance, conduct or suitability.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Prompt-level test suite including adversarial phrasing and prompt-injection attempts

business_rules.statement: Every measurement in the register carries all fifteen governance attributes with no blank.
No run with an offline assigned device inside the connectivity window is auto-cancelled.
Zero transitions occur inside a legal-hold scope.
No anonymisation occurs in a Regulated-Industry tenant.
The hold check is per object, not per batch.
Every occurrence re-reads all eight gate conditions at execution time and never uses a creation-time snapshot for an authority, qualification, hold or version decision.

Pure database polling with no queue and no managed trigger
Single durable workflow engine for everything
Batch orchestrator as the platform scheduler

options: Skip
Execute once
Replay individually
Aggregate
Expire
Human review
Adopt durable workflow engine at V1
Defer durable workflow engine
decisions.impact: Determines what happens to every moment missed during an outage or a deployment; owner: client platform team.

decisions.question: Backfill and replay authority, bounds and review triggers; separately, the customer-hosted parity commitment.
options: Relational-database-backed queue using row-level claim with skip-locked reads
Self-hosted broker
Adapter per mechanism

decisions.question: Lease duration, heartbeat interval and fencing-token semantics; separately, the provider and cost envelope.
decisions.impact: Determines how quickly a crashed worker's work is picked up and how a late write is refused.

decisions.question: Retry limits, spacing and dead-letter thresholds per class; separately, the Super Admin scheduler registry screens and scheduled-obligation strip.
options: Fixed small count with exponential backoff
Count that varies by authority class

decisions.impact: Determines whether a transient failure is absorbed or amplified.

decisions.question: Daylight-saving, month-end and time-zone-change behaviour for local-clock schedules; separately, Recovery Time Objective, Recovery Point Objective and poll interval.
options: Fire once at the first instant after the spring-forward gap
Fire on the first occurrence of a repeated local time and record the second as a suppressed duplicate
Fire on the last day of a shorter month
Treat leap day as an ordinary day
decisions.adopted_working_position: Behaviours proposed for confirmation; occurrences already materialised keep their planned instants when a Site time zone changes
decisions.impact: Determines behaviour on the two irregular days a year and at every month end.

decisions.question: Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective for the scheduling control plane; separately, retry and dead-letter limits, queue receive count and command validity period.
options: Frequent point-in-time recovery, RPO in minutes, higher cost
Daily snapshots, RPO in hours, lower cost
Tiered posture: audit and evidence get option (a), derived aggregates get option (b)
decisions.impact: Determines what the platform may promise about coming back after a failure; owner: client.

decisions.question: Observability thresholds for scheduled work including stuck-state ages, missed-run detection latency and backlog limits; separately, aligning a durable workflow engine's own history retention with the platform retention model.
options: Fixed absolute threshold
Multiple of the definition's normal cadence
Service-level objective with an error budget
decisions.impact: Determines how quickly a silent scheduler is noticed; owner: client platform team.

decisions.question: Drift-canary cadence and its named owner's cover arrangements; separately, whether any individual-level productivity measurement is ever permitted and what the minimum-population suppression threshold is.

No individual-level productivity measurement at V1

decisions.impact: Determines how long a degraded agent can act before anyone knows, and the worker-privacy boundary.

decisions.question: Cadence, batching and maintenance-window interaction for the tiering, anonymisation and trace-retention schedulers; separately, the observability product stack and operational ownership and escalation.
options: Prometheus-compatible metrics
OpenTelemetry instrumentation
Grafana-style dashboard layer
On-call paging service

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The control plane running but producing no effects, for example because every claim is refused by a stuck lease table. Detection is receipt absence against planned occurrences within a tolerance that is TBD under DEC-SCHED-008.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Automatic lease expiry and re-claim
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Leases cannot expire; second fallback is an operator-initiated lease break, a governed privileged action, followed by re-claim with a higher fencing token
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The scheduler is stopped deliberately and every affected item is listed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A bounded backfill under section 45A.8

failures_fallbacks.trigger: State-machine drift, where an occurrence sits in a non-terminal state indefinitely because no transition applies. Detection is an age threshold per state, TBD under DEC-SCHED-008.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Automatic transition to quarantined with the stuck state recorded
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Quarantining also fails; second fallback is an operator listing of stuck occurrences produced directly from the durable rows
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The occurrence remains visible in its stuck state and no effect is attempted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A governed release or cancellation; reconciliation records the stuck period and its resolution

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Authority drift: a non-human identity accumulating permissions beyond its definitions' declared scopes. Detection is a permission-difference report.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Automatic narrowing to the union of active definition scopes
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Narrowing would break a running definition; second fallback is to pause that definition and raise it for review rather than keep the broad grant
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The identity holds no permission and no scheduled effect occurs
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A corrected definition and a re-approved scope; reconciliation re-runs the difference report and reviews every effect performed while the excess permission existed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A card that has drifted from the definition it describes, most plausibly after a revision changed a policy without a card update. Detection is a field-by-field comparison at every approval and on a recurring integrity check.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Block approval until the card matches
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A mismatch on an already-active definition; second fallback is to pause the definition rather than accept the card as advisory
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The definition paused and its occurrences suppressed but visible
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A corrected card and a re-approval; reconciliation compares every card against every active revision

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A catch-up storm after a long outage: a backlog executes at once, floods the two notification channels and spikes load. Detection is a backlog-size threshold, TBD under DEC-SCHED-008.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Automatic collapse and spacing under the five storm controls
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Backlog still exceeds the concurrency limits; second fallback is to suspend catch-up entirely and list the backlog for a governed backfill decision
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No catch-up executes and the entire backlog is listed with its ages
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A bounded, approved backfill in priority order, with irreversible and externally visible work reviewed individually

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Scheduler unavailable - the trigger layer produces no tick. Detection is an absence alert on the definition's expected-run heartbeat plus a query for occurrences past due_at.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The secondary trigger source on a different failure domain emits the tick; a Platform Engineer may issue a governed manual tick
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Neither trigger fires and no operator is available
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Backlog accumulates; nothing is marked done; the ledger preserves intended times
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Trigger restored; sweep drains in due-time order; each occurrence re-runs the eight-condition gate at its actual execution time, not at its intended time

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Ledger or database unavailable - the authority layer cannot be read or written. Detection is connection failures on the sweep and health probes.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Connection retry with backoff, bounded; then a read replica for rendering, clearly labelled as possibly stale
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Replica also unavailable; there is no alternate authority, by design
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Controlled stop of all scheduled execution. No occurrence executes, so no false record is written
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Restore; verify ledger, outbox and audit log restore to a mutually consistent point; occurrences between the restore point and the failure are re-derived from the outbox and audit log rather than blindly re-run

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Duplicate execution - two workers, or two ticks, execute the same occurrence. Detection is the unique constraint on the idempotency key rejecting the second write; the rejection is counted, not swallowed.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The unique constraint itself; the second attempt terminates as duplicate_suppressed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The constraint is missing, which is a defect caught by TEST-SCHED-122-01 before deployment
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: If a double effect landed, the affected records are quarantined for Quality Manager review; nothing is deleted
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Compensating action, recorded; one effect, two audit rows

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Missed occurrence (misfire) - the due time passed and nothing ran. Detection is absence alerting.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The next sweep; then catch-up per the definition's catch-up policy
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The catch-up policy says do not catch up, for example a stale suspension whose commercial cause has since been resolved
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The occurrence is recorded as missed with a reason, never silently dropped
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Human decision on whether to re-issue; reauthorization and revalidation are mandatory before any catch-up execution

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Catch-up storm - the scheduler returns after a long outage and thousands of occurrences are due at once. Detection is backlog depth crossing its threshold and sweep claim rate saturating.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Rate-limited draining in due-time order with per-tenant fairness, so one large tenant cannot starve the others
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Draining is slower than new work arrives
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Back-pressure - the sweep stops claiming new occurrences beyond a concurrency ceiling and the backlog remains visible rather than being discarded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Capacity added; drain completes; deduplication by idempotency key

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Poison occurrence - one occurrence fails deterministically every time and consumes a worker. Detection is attempt count crossing the configured limit, value TBD under DEC-SCHED-007.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Move to the dead-letter store, which is a table in the ledger, not only a queue
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The dead-letter store is unmonitored, which is why dead-letter depth greater than zero is an alert, not a metric
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The occurrence is quarantined with its payload preserved for diagnosis; no partial effect exists because the handler is transactional
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Defect fixed; governed redrive; final state failed then succeeded_after_redrive or cancelled_with_reason

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Handler bug producing a wrong effect. Detection is invariant checks after execution, for example a finished run whose summary was never computed, or a tiering transition inside a legal-hold scope.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Halt the definition immediately, a governed control on the Super Admin console; retrying a wrong effect produces two wrong effects
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The halt is applied after many occurrences already ran
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Affected records quarantined for Quality Manager review; the platform never deletes, so every wrong effect is reversible by compensation
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Compensating actions executed as a governed batch with maker-checker; the compensation batch requires its own approval; material corrections flagged in the next scheduled report delivery

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Clock or time-zone error on the platform - an occurrence fires at the wrong local time. Detection is comparison of intended local time against the Site's timezone anchor.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The definition's timezone is re-resolved from the Site record rather than from a server default
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Site has no timezone, which cannot occur because a Site carries the timezone by definition
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The definition is halted rather than firing at an unknown local time
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Fix and re-run with correct local semantics; digest deliveries at the wrong hour are re-sent with an explanation, never silently duplicated

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Tenant suspended between scheduling and execution - a soft, hard or compliance suspension applies. Detection is the gate's tenant-scope and authority checks reading current suspension state.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Execute only the portion permitted by the suspension state - notably, run auto-close continues under hard suspension because record closure is explicitly part of the completion pipeline
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The permitted portion cannot be isolated
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Block with reason; the record stays open; the Tenant Admin sees the banner appropriate to their state
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On suspension release, blocked occurrences are re-gated and executed; DEC-SUSP-001 contradiction preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Legal hold placed after an occurrence was scheduled - tiering, anonymisation or erasure would violate the hold. Detection is gate condition 6, evaluated at execution time and never at scheduling time.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The occurrence is deferred, not cancelled, and re-evaluated when the hold is released
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The hold register is unreadable, which is gate condition 6 failing
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Nothing tiers, nothing anonymises, nothing erases. Because anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act, its safe state is always inaction
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Hold released by dual approval; deferred occurrences re-gated; the deferral period is recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command cannot reach the device. Detection is command age and device last-seen.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Connectivity-loss protocol at 30, 60 and 120 minutes
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Device never returns
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Offline trust window expiry; the command stays queued and visibly undelivered; manual close of a stuck run remains available to a Supervisor as an audited act
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Per 45A.11 - device returns or is retired through the fleet module; pending commands cancelled with a reason and tombstoned

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Notification fails to send or fails to be delivered - the platform-contracted email vendor is unavailable, or an address bounces. Detection is provider rejection, bounce, or absence of provider acceptance.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Bounded resend attempts, then the in-app channel, which cannot be muted and is therefore the more reliable of the only two channels the platform has
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Both channels fail
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The underlying obligation is unaffected, because a notification is never the mechanism enforcing anything. A qualification block still blocks; a hold still holds
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Vendor restored; the notification is re-sent with its original context and an explanation of the delay

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Artificial-intelligence dependency unavailable during a scheduled agent run - the Shift Handoff Agent's run 30 minutes before shift end cannot complete. Detection is agent-run failure or timeout; second consecutive failure or any failure outlasting a shift escalates.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: One bounded retry inside the remaining pre-shift window, then a deterministic non-agentic handover summary assembled from the record: open anomalies, holds in force, runs in each state, unacknowledged escalations
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The deterministic summary also cannot be assembled, which means the record store is unavailable, which is F2
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The outgoing supervisor is told plainly that no brief was produced and is prompted to complete a manual handover; the handoff obligation is not marked satisfied
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Agent restored; the brief is produced for the record with a clear late marker; it is not back-dated

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Cross-tenant leakage risk in a batch occurrence - an aggregation job's scope is wrong. Detection is a scope assertion inside the handler comparing every row's tenant identifier against the declared scope, plus the enforced anonymisation invariant in the data path.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Halt the definition; a scope failure is never retried, because retrying a leak is a second leak
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Output already produced
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Output quarantined and unpublished; the incident treated as a security event under the client's own process
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Defect fixed; output recomputed; any downstream artefact derived from the bad output is invalidated

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Authority revoked between scheduling and execution - the approver who authorised the future act no longer holds the role. Detection is gate condition 2 at execution time.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Route to the current holder of the required role for a fresh decision; where nobody holds it on shift, escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery (DEC-NOSHIFT-001)
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No holder exists at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The obligation remains open and visibly overdue; this state should be structurally unreachable and if reached indicates a data-integrity defect that must be surfaced
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Role assigned; obligation re-gated; the gap is recorded

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Version changed between scheduling and execution - a new workflow version published. Detection is gate condition 4.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None needed - pinning is the answer; the in-flight run continues on its pinned version
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run finishes on the version it started on
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The per-device package inventory records which package version each run executed against; DEC-LIB-001 contradiction preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Storage or retention occurrence attempts a prohibited deletion - a misconfigured lifecycle rule. Detection is the infrastructure policy scan at deployment and a runtime assertion in the tiering handler.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Halt
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Objects already expired - the one failure this platform genuinely cannot compensate, because deletion is the only irreversible operation besides anonymisation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Restore from backup, which is the reason the backup obligation is not optional
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Restore, verify, report; an unintended deletion is recorded as an incident, not as an erasure certificate

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Recovery after a human already completed the action - the scheduler was down, a person did the job by hand, and then the scheduler came back and did it again. Detection is an idempotency key derived from the business outcome, not from the occurrence identifier.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The business-outcome idempotency check
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The check is absent for an obligation whose outcome is hard to key, for example send a digest
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: For un-keyable obligations, the occurrence executes and the duplicate is visible and explained to the recipient rather than suppressed on a guess. Honest duplication beats a silent gap
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The manual action is recorded in the same ledger as a manual_completion row so the next occurrence can see it; where outcomes differ, the later is not automatically preferred and a Quality Manager decides

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A mechanism is selected that cannot satisfy an obligation discovered later, for example a queue whose maximum delay is shorter than the business wait required. Detection is the register's maximum supported wait and payload columns plus TEST-SCHED-009-02.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Promote the definition to the next mechanism class up the authority ladder (queue delay to application-owned scheduler to durable workflow engine) without changing the handler
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No mechanism class supports the requirement, for instance a wait measured in years combined with a cancellation requirement
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The definition is marked not automatable at V1 and converted to mechanism class M12, governed manual operation, with a named owner and a calendar obligation. It is never silently downgraded to best effort
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The requirement enters the roadmap with a DEC-SCHED-* card; the manual operation continues and is audited

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A mechanism class is used outside its stated never for column, for example M8 used for run auto-close. Detection is the register lint TEST-SCHED-095-01 cross-checking authority class against mechanism class.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Move the definition to M5 and keep the handler byte-identical
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: M5 is itself unavailable, covered as F1
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The obligation is not executed and is visibly overdue on every surface that shows it; nothing is marked done
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The sweep resumes and processes the backlog in due-time order with the original intended times preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Two surfaces disagree about an occurrence, for example the Client Command Center shows a hold in force while the Delivery Operations Hub shows it propagating. Detection is a consistency probe comparing rendered state against ledger state per surface on a cadence.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Delivery Operations Hub's record wins and the other surface re-fetches
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The disagreement persists, indicating a real divergence rather than a rendering lag
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The Client Command Center renders the element as state uncertain, last confirmed at with its timestamp and disables any action that depends on the uncertain state. It never picks the optimistic reading
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconcile against the ledger and the command record; where a human acted on the wrong reading, the audited-recompute rule applies and the correction is flagged

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A scheduled activation fires while its approval is no longer valid, for example the Release Authority's role was removed. Detection is the due-moment re-validation.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Block and notify the Job Owner and the Release Authority role
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Nobody acts and the content never becomes effective
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The previous version remains in force. Runs continue on a version that was fully approved - the platform's default is the last-known-good approved mode
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-approve or re-schedule; the activation attempt, its block reason and its eventual outcome are all recorded against the version

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The push channel to the Client Command Center stalls, so scheduled-occurrence events do not arrive. Detection is the surface tracking its own last-event time against the expected heartbeat; the freshness marker ages visibly.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Fall back from pushed to refreshed, polling at the tenant's refresh interval, default 60 seconds and floor 30 seconds
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Polling also fails
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The board displays its last known picture with a prominent age, and every action control that depends on current state is disabled with the reason shown. It does not blank, and it does not pretend
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Channel restored; the surface re-fetches state rather than replaying a backlog of events, so it converges rather than flickering

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The device clock is grossly wrong - a user set it manually, or the hardware clock lost power. Detection is the skew guard at sync and locally by monotonic-clock inconsistency between boots.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The device widens its uncertainty margin and resolves toward the restrictive outcome
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device cannot establish any trustworthy time reference at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device treats the offline trust window as exhausted, requires a sync before designated high-risk actions and sign-offs, and continues to allow ordinary work whose safety does not depend on time. It does not brick itself
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On sync the server sets the offset, re-stamps ordering by server-receipt time, and clears the skew flag once inside the threshold

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The console's telemetry pipeline lags, so backlog figures are stale and the platform team believes the schedulers are healthy. Detection is each telemetry figure carrying its own as-of time with a staleness alert.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Direct query against the ledger for the affected definitions, bypassing the aggregation layer but not the access model
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The ledger is itself unreachable, which is the correlated database outage
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The console renders scheduler health unknown since 04:12 rather than a green indicator. A green indicator computed from stale data is the single most dangerous rendering on this surface
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Pipeline restored; figures recomputed; the staleness incident recorded; any governed control exercised during the stale window is reviewed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The metrics pipeline stops. Detection is a synthetic heartbeat metric whose absence is itself alerted, plus staleness checks on every dashboard panel.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Direct ledger queries, slower but authoritative
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The ledger is unavailable, which is F2
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Dashboards render unknown since rather than a green state; alerting falls back to ledger-derived checks at a lower frequency
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Pipeline restored; a gap is visible in the charts and is not back-filled with fabricated points; audit evidence is unaffected throughout

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Alerts do not fire because the alerting system is down. Detection is a dead-man's-switch alert - a signal that fires if a periodic heartbeat stops.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Secondary alerting path on an independent channel
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Both paths down
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Scheduled work continues correctly but unobserved; the platform is fragile rather than broken. An unobserved failure still does not produce a false record
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Restore alerting; review the unobserved window for missed incidents by querying the ledger directly; any incident that occurred unobserved is written up retrospectively

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A scheduled process is written that materialises a per-worker behavioural aggregate. Detection is the measurement register lint plus a data-model assertion that no persisted table has a worker identifier as a grouping key for a behavioural measure.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The definition is refused at review
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: It ships
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The table is dropped, the definition is disabled, and an incident is raised under the client's privacy process
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Rebuild at the correct granularity; determine whether any output was distributed and to whom, and notify

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Someone assembles a disciplinary case by querying the audit log. Detection is that audit-log access is itself audited and a query pattern reading many rows for one worker across a long period is a detectable signal.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The access requires a named purpose and an approval
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The access is legitimate on its face but used for a prohibited purpose, which no technical control can fully prevent
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The prohibited-uses list is contractual as well as technical. The platform can make surveillance hard, it cannot make it impossible, and the client must close the gap in policy
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Through the client's own process; the client's employment-data policy is TBD - Client Decision Required

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An artificial-intelligence output is used as input to an employment decision. Detection is not technically detectable inside the platform.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Every agent output carries a visible statement of its advisory status and its prohibited uses
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The statement is ignored
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The prohibition is contractual, is reflected in the EU Artificial Intelligence Act Article 14 human-oversight narrative the source already carries, and must appear in the client's terms with tenants
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Policy enforcement outside the platform

failures_fallbacks.trigger: One of the twelve scheduled-work prohibitions is violated in code. Detection is the ten-question gate implemented as an architecture-decision checklist plus automated checks - a lint for timer application programming interfaces in Client Command Center code, a lint for storage lifecycle expiration rules, a contract test for handler idempotency.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The change is blocked at review
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: It reaches production
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected definition is moved to mechanism class M12, governed manual operation, until fixed; the obligation is performed by a named human and audited
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Fix, re-test, restore automation; audit the period of violation for double or missed effects and correct through the audited-recompute rule

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An automation ships without a nineteen-point assessment. Detection is the register lint requiring all nineteen points per definition.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The definition is blocked from the register and therefore from deployment
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: It ships anyway through an unregistered path
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The unregistered definition is disabled on discovery and its effects reviewed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Assess and re-register; review the period of unassessed operation for wrong effects

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A vendor changes documented behaviour, for example tightening or loosening delivery semantics. Detection is an annual mechanism-register review plus a contract test asserting the assumed semantics empirically rather than trusting documentation.
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The platform's own guarantees do not move, because they are built on the ledger, not on the vendor
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A vendor behaviour change breaks the adapter contract
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected obligations fall back to mechanism class M5
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-baseline the register; any occurrence executed during the ambiguity window is checked against the ledger for double effect
